summary: The blueprint broadly covers healthy human pancreas but needs targeted vascular/stromal refinement and minor module-label hygiene.

issues.description: Blood endothelium is represented only as a module and as the negative side of the lymphatic endothelial axis; there is no positive axis directly resolving blood or fenestrated pancreatic endothelial identity.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a gated endothelial_blood_identity or endothelial_fenestrated_capillary axis using endothelial as the gate, with blood_endothelial or a refined capillary/fenestrated module as the positive module and lymphatic_endothelial as a negative module.

issues.description: The fibroblast_stellate module includes RGS5, a strong mural/pericyte marker already used in vascular_mural, which can blur stromal and perivascular axes.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace RGS5 in fibroblast_stellate with a fibroblast/stellate-enriched marker such as FBLN1, COL15A1, C7, MFAP5, MMP2, CXCL14, or a quiescent stellate/retinoid-associated marker.

issues.description: The stromal branch has broad fibroblast/stellate identity and activated myofibroblast axes, but does not clearly resolve quiescent pancreatic stellate cells, an expected healthy-pancreas stromal state.
issues.suggested_fix: Refine fibroblast_stellate to better represent quiescent stellate biology, or add a gated quiescent stellate/retinoid-storage axis under fibroblast_stellate using markers such as RBP1, LRAT, PDGFRB, COL6A1, VIM, and matrix fibroblast markers, contrasted against activated_stellate_myofibroblast.

issues.description: The b_plasma_cell module contains canonical B-cell genes and is separate from the plasma_cell module, so the current label implies a mixed B/plasma program that the markers do not actually encode.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the biological content but adjust labels/names in place if possible to b_cell and immune_b_cell, while retaining the separate plasma_cell module and axis.

out_of_scope: Further subdivision of T cells into CD4, CD8, and regulatory T cells would be useful for an immune-focused atlas but is not required for this broad healthy-pancreas embedding.
Rare inflammatory granulocytes are not essential for a baseline healthy pancreas blueprint unless downstream datasets are expected to contain substantial blood or inflamed tissue.
